SUMMARY JUDGMENT
Now comes Defendant Sellie Echols and respectfully moves this Court pursuant to Rule 56 of the Ohio Rules of Civil Procedure for judgment in her favor and against Defendant Robert Echols on the Crossclaim on the grounds that there are no genuine issues of material fact and Movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law.
In support of this Motion, Movant submits the following Memorandum in Support and evidentiary materials.
Respectfully submitted,
/s/ E. Daniel Mamrack E. DANIEL MAMRACK, #0018119 Attorney for Defendant Sellie Echols 33977 Chardon Road, Suite 100 Willoughby Hills, OH 44094 440-516-0200 440-585-1680 facsimile edmatty@sbcglobal.net

MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT
Defendant Sellie Echols ("Sellie") is the owner of and resides in the property at 11389 Clark Road in Chardon Township (the "Property"). Defendant Robert Echols ("Robert") resides at 11347 Clark Road, just to the west of Sellie's home.
Plaintiffs have filed a Complaint on behalf of the Geauga County Board of Health seeking enforcement of a Board of Health Order issued against Sellie, and on behalf of Chardon Township seeking enforcement of township zoning regulations. This action essentially seeks to prohibit Robert from continuing to operate his salvage business on the Property and the clean-up of the Property. Sellie filed a Crossclaim against Robert seeking reimbursement for any and all costs, expenses and damages which she may suffer as a result of Plaintiff's claims.
Robert previously filed suit against Sellie concerning the Property, being Robert Echols vs. Sellie Echols, Geauga County Common Pleas Case No. 20M000246. On March 19, 2021, this Court found that Robert's actions constituted waste, and entered an Order and of Ejectment against Robert. Robert has failed to comply with the Order, and in fact has increased his unauthorized and illegal operations at and on the Property. A copy of the relevant portion of the Order is attached hereto. And see Affidavit of Robin Echols attached.
As noted in the affidavit of Robin Echols, as well as the Order issued by Geauga County, Robert has accumulated a massive collection of scrap and other material on the Property. Further, despite demand Plaintiff refuses to comply with the Order issued by the Geauga County Board of Healthy, Chardon Township, or the Order of Ejectment issued by this Court and in fact has increased the level of the prohibited conduct.
CONCLUSION
Rule 56 of the Ohio Rules of Civil Procedure sets forth the conditions for granting a motion for summary judgment. In order for summary judgment to be granted, “. .. it must be determined that: (1) no genuine issue as to any material fact remains to be litigated; (2) the
2

moving party is entitled to judgment as a matter of law; and (3) it appears from the evidence that reasonable minds can come to but one conclusion, and in viewing such evidence most strongly in favor of the party against whom the motion for summary judgment is made, that conclusion is adverse to that party." Temple v. Wean United, Inc., 50 Ohio St.2d 317, 364 N.E.2d 267, 274 (1977).
As set forth above, there is no issue as to any material fact remaining to be litigated and as a matter of law Defendant Sellie Echols is entitled to judgment in her favor on the Crossclaim. It is undisputed that Robert by operating his salvage business on the Property, is solely responsible for the actions and conduct which has resulted in the issuance of the Order by the Geauga County Board of Health and the violation of the zoning ordinances of Chardon Township, and his continued operation of the salvage business thereafter, in violation of the County and Township orders and the Order of Ejectment previously issued by this Court, is the sole reason this action has been brought by Plaintiffs. As a result, Defendant Sellie Echols is entitled to judgment against Robert for any and all costs, expenses and damages which she may suffer as a result of the any judgement entered in Plaintiffs' favor on Complaint and proceedings thereafter on the judgment, the amount of such costs, expenses and damages to be determined at that time.
Respectfully submitted.
/s/ E. Daniel Mamrack E. DANIEL MAMRACK Attorney for Defendant Sellie Echols 33977 Chardon Road, Suite 100 Willoughby Hills, OH 44094 440-516-0200 440-585-1680 facsimile edmatty@sbcglobal.net

SELLIE ECHOLS,
DECISION AND JUDGMENT
Defendant.
This matter came on for consideration of Defendant Sellie Echols' "Motion for Summary Judgment" ("MSJ") filed January 8, 2021. Although the MSJ initially states "Defendant . . . moves ... for judgment in her favor on the Counterclaim," both the Complaint and Counterclaim are discussed in the MSJ and Defendant requests "judgment in her favor on the complaint and for judgment against the Plaintiff ejecting him."
On January 22, 2021, "Plaintiff's Response to Defendant's Motion for Summary Judgment" was filed. Plaintiff argued against the MSJ as to both the complaint and the counterclaim.
On February 4, 2021, "Defendant's Reply Brief" was filed.
The Court finds defendant has moved for summary judgment on both the complaint and the counterclaim. See Civ.R. 1(B).
I. Procedural facts.
On March 30, 2020, plaintiff Robert L. Echols, Jr. ("Mr. Echols") filed a four count verified complaint: (1) Promissory estoppel-Specific performance; (2) Breach of Contract; (3) Intentional fraud; and (4) Unjust enrichment.
1

Ms. Echols received some benefit from Mr. Echols; however, she conferred even more benefit on Mr. Echols. Ms. Echols met her initial burden, establishing she has not been unjustly enriched by Mr. Echols. Mr. Echols failed to provide rebuttal evidence.
C. Ms. Echols' counterclaim for ejectment: R.C. 5303.03.
"In an action for the recovery of real property, it is sufficient if the plaintiff states in his petition that he has a legal estate therein and is entitled to the possession thereof, describing it with such certainty as to identify the property, and that the defendant unlawfully keeps him out of the possession. It is not necessary to state how the plaintiff's estate or ownership is derived." R.C. 5303.03.
To obtain possession of land held adversely by defendants, the plaintiff must "produce evidence of a better legal estate or title." Avery v. Avery, 107 Ohio App. 199, 202, 157 N.E.2d 917 (6th Dist. 1958)
Ejectment and forcible entry and detainer are specific and distinct statutory remedies. See Gvozdanovic v. Woodford Corp., 139 Ohio App.3d 11, 16, 742 N.E.2d 1145 (1st Dist.2000); Bond v. Frost, 57 O.O. 360, 125 N.E.2d 379 (C.P.1955) paragraph 2 of the syllabus; compare R.C. Ch. 1923 and 5303.03. A legal title may be enforced through an ejectment action. See Avery v. Avery, 107 Ohio App. 199, 204, 157 N.E.2d 917 (6th Dist.1958).
Ms. Echols bears the burden of establishing title. Since her legal ownership is undisputed, Ms. Echols has met her initial summary judgment burden.
In rebuttal, Mr. Echols established Ms. Echols made various promises, permitted Mr. Echols to enter onto and use a portion of her Property, and allowed him to make payments directly to her mortgagee.
17

Ms. Echols established while Mr. Echols may have paid rent or other monies to her mortgagee, Mr. Echols defaulted in these payments, expanded the area of use beyond what she permitted, and committed waste upon the Property.
Ms. Echols showed she is entitled to an Order returning her Property to her.6
Judgment.
Defendant Sellie Echols' "Motion for Summary Judgment" is granted. She is granted judgment both on Plaintiff's Verified Complaint and on her Counterclaim.
Plaintiff Robert L. Echols, Jr. is ordered to pay the costs of this action.
IT IS SO ORDERED.
CAROLYN J. PASCHKE, JUDGE
6 Ms. Echols did not specifically request money damages but they may be available for injury to the Property.
